races.paceDynamic: So Smart will take them along from the front, with Call Time and Macarone likely to track close behind in the early stages. The confirmed front runner So Smart should get an uncontested lead given the lack of other natural pace-setters, allowing him to dictate terms through steady fractions. This sets up a tactical affair where the pace will likely build gradually rather than being truly run throughout. The sustainable pace and lack of early pressure strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If So Smart gets an easy lead without early pressure
scenarios.body: The seven-year-old can control the race from the front and kick clear when the pace lifts in the final furlong. His recent third over course and distance when leading long shows he handles this exact scenario well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time or other prominent runners get the perfect stalking position behind So Smart
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows trackers to conserve energy before unleashing their finish, with Call Time's course and distance win proving his effectiveness in this tactical setup. The sustained gallop plays to horses who can quicken from prominent positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes even slower than expected in the middle stages
scenarios.body: The lack of early speed allows hold-up horses like Some Nightmare and Hidden Verse to get closer than usual before making their moves. Some Nightmare's three course and distance wins show he can excel when getting the right tactical race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Speed Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If So Smart goes too fast early or gets pressured by multiple prominent runners
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly strong pace could set up the race for a closer with tactical speed, though this seems unlikely given the field composition. The veteran Some Nightmare could benefit most from such a collapse.

watchPoints.text: So Smart must be monitored for any early pressure from Call Time or Macarone that could compromise his front-running tactics
Call Time's fitness after 62 days off and trainer's poor recent form could see him fade if the pace lifts late
Some Nightmare needs the pace to develop right for his hold-up style and any strong early gallop would compromise his chances
Fletcher's Flight's tendency to race too freely could see him waste energy early and compromise his finishing kick
Pearl's Edge returning from seven months off makes any market support significant given the extended absence

races.paceDynamic: Poetry Of Time, Island Bear, and Aigeas will engage from the off in this 7-runner affair, creating a strong gallop that will test stamina credentials over the 7f trip on testing ground. Poetry Of Time looks the most professional of the pace angle having won comfortably last time, while Island Bear showed decent pace positioning recently and Aigeas needs to bounce back but has early speed. The sustained pace will suit prominent racers like Mighty Vega and Lyra Lea who can track the leaders without getting embroiled in the early battle. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners who can sit close enough to strike but avoid the pace duel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Poetry Of Time and Island Bear go too hard early and Mighty Vega or Lyra Lea track them perfectly
scenarios.body: The leaders will tie up in the soft ground allowing the prominent runners to strike with superior finishing kicks. Mighty Vega's recent Lingfield win and Lyra Lea's solid return suggest they can capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Poetry Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Poetry Of Time gets an uncontested lead or settles the pace on his terms
scenarios.body: The Haggas runner can use his class advantage and proven 7f form to control from the front and kick clear. His comfortable Salisbury win suggests he has more in hand than this mark.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than anticipated and all three leaders weaken significantly
scenarios.body: Ebn Sabt from his hold-up position could pick up the pieces despite his poor recent form. The 7lb claimer and drop back from longer trips might help his cause.

scenarios.title: Island Bear Springs Surprise

scenarios.body: The Newland runner could use his early pace to steal a march turning for home before the others respond. His recent Nottingham fifth wasn't without merit and the headgear change adds hope.

races.paceDynamic: Terries Royale, Receipt, and Connie's Rose will ensure a strong gallop from the off, with Bela Sonata also likely to be handy early. Receipt has shown tendencies to race keenly and fade, while Terries Royale is on a poor run but will still lead them along at a decent clip. This strong pace will set up the race perfectly for the hold-up horses to pick off the pace-setters in the closing stages. The combination of soft going and a guaranteed strong gallop heavily favours horses with finishing kicks who can sit off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters go too hard early and tire in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop will stretch the field and allow the closers to pick them off with superior finishing speed on the testing ground. Horses like Kisskodi, Bold Impact, and Under The Twilight are perfectly positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but sustainable, allowing handy horses to kick clear
scenarios.body: This Farh and Dapper Gee Gee can use their prominent positions to strike at the right moment without getting caught up in the early speed battle. Their tactical positioning gives them the perfect launching pad.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Course specialist strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Connie's Rose can dictate from the front at a more measured tempo
scenarios.body: Her intimate knowledge of the track allows her to control the race from the front, using her seven previous course wins to maximum advantage. She can slow things down just enough to have something left for the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If all the front-runners go off too conservatively and it becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace would turn this into a dash from the 2f marker, suiting horses with natural speed regardless of their usual tactics. Even the hold-up horses would struggle in a slowly-run race that becomes all about acceleration.

Terries Royale has failed to beat a rival in his last run and the cheekpieces reapplication suggests connections are concerned
This Farh carries a 3lb penalty for his recent Beverley win but his current momentum could overcome the extra weight
Connie's Rose faces a quick turnaround of just 8 days since her narrow defeat at this course and distance

races.paceDynamic: Judge Frank is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, with Eye Of The Water likely to track him in second. The pace will be moderate rather than fierce given the lack of early pace pressure, allowing Judge Frank to control the rhythm through the first three quarters. With 8 of the 10 runners having hold-up or midfield styles, this creates a bunched finish where stamina and tactical positioning become crucial. This pace setup clearly favours prominent racers and those with proven tactical speed, as the lack of early pace will make it difficult for pure hold-up horses to find the necessary gaps in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Judge Frank gets an easy lead and Eye Of The Water tracks comfortably
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows the front pair to maintain their advantage as the hold-up brigade struggle for room in a bunched finish. Judge Frank's recent wins came from prominent positions and he gets the ideal scenario here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Class
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and allows superior RPR horses to close
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates perfect conditions for Fifty Sent and Judge Frank to use their higher ratings in a sprint finish. Both have shown they can quicken when the tempo lifts late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins Out
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched field creates a messy finish with limited room
scenarios.body: Eye Of The Water's prominent style gives him the best position while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic behind the leading pair. His recent AW form suggests he retains enough ability at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to fire and the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: The slow tempo allows a patient ride on Mooretown Lad or the step up in trip suits A Rose Adaay perfectly. Both have shown glimpses of ability and could benefit from the tactical nature.

watchPoints.text: Judge Frank could get too easy a lead if Eye Of The Water doesn't track close enough, making him very hard to peg back
Liberty Bird bled from the nose when pulled up last time and any respiratory issues could see her struggle again
Praise Indeed faces a 324-day absence and needs to prove her fitness after switching trainers since last seen
Eye Of The Water's prominent style could be crucial if the field bunches up and hold-up horses get trapped
Fifty Sent has the highest rating but 49 days off and hold-up style may not suit the likely tactical scenario

races.name: V3 UK- Principal Contractor Handicap (Chepstow Mile Series Qualifier) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist but all wins on AW surfaces and 32 days off suggest fitness concerns on return to turf
runners_data.comment: All six wins have been on AW; cheekpieces return but he doesn't convince.
runners_data.spotlight: All six wins have been on AW; cheekpieces return but he doesn't convince.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who thrives in tactical scenarios and has strong place record in similar contests
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent but doesn't win too often; hasn't been far away of late.
runners_data.spotlight: Generally consistent but doesn't win too often; hasn't been far away of late and regularly makes the frame; has place claims.

runners_data.name: Homeland
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter returning after 187 days off but previously effective over longer trips and holds tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Fifth on stable debut at Wolverhampton in December; unraced since but on a decent mark.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored for Michael Dods at Ripon (1m2f, good) last July off 5lb higher; sold to join current yard for 4,000gns in October; fifth of 12 on stable debut at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) in December; unraced since but on a decent mark.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 285 days absence since last August raises serious fitness doubts despite solid 2023 form
runners_data.comment: Last of two wins came in September 2022; seemed to find his level again last year.
runners_data.spotlight: Last of two wins came in September 2022; seemed to find his level again last year when making the frame four times; has been absent since last August though and needs to hit the ground running.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose mark has dropped significantly and could benefit from patient ride in tactical affair
runners_data.comment: His losing run goes back to July 2024 and his mark has plummeted since.
runners_data.spotlight: His losing run goes back to July 2024 and his mark has plummeted since but he could build on April's fifth at Nottingham; not discounted.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Sunrise
runners_data.note: Eight-race maiden with strong recent AW form but unproven on turf in handicap company
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden but has shown he can find a race; best effort was when beaten a nose at Kempton (1m, AW) in January and if can replicate that form on turf then he comes into the equation; has left Pat Phelan since his last run in March; sports a first-time tongue-tie and has to be of interest for new yard.

runners_data.name: Nutcracker
runners_data.note: Eleven-race maiden showing improvement in classified events but needs to transfer AW form to turf handicaps
runners_data.comment: 11-race maiden but has gone close in classifieds at Wolverhampton on his last two starts.
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden but has gone close in classified events at Wolverhampton (8.5, AW) on his last two starts; needs to convert that form to handicaps on turf.

runners_data.name: Marisitta
runners_data.note: Inconsistent maiden with cheekpieces returning but lacks conviction and hard to trust in competitive field
runners_data.comment: Still a maiden and lacks consistency to boot.
runners_data.spotlight: Still a maiden and lacks consistency to boot; returning cheekpieces replace first-time hood worn last time; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Uncle Albert
runners_data.note: Hold-up type making stable debut but poor recent form and tendency to fade in finish raises concerns
runners_data.comment: Sole success came in March 2024 when trained in Ireland; makes his British/stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in March 2024 when trained by Kieran Cotter in Ireland; has lost his way this year and makes his British/stable debut; probably best watched for now.

races.paceDynamic: Homeland appears the lone confirmed early leader, with Rival potentially joining him in the early positions given his prominent tendencies. With just 9 runners and minimal pace pressure, Homeland can dictate a measured gallop through the first half-mile on this testing soft ground. The lack of genuine speed horses means this will develop into a tactical affair with the real race beginning in the final 3 furlongs. This moderate pace scenario heavily favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish, as the leaders will have plenty left for a kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Homeland sets uncontested fractions and the pace is steady throughout
scenarios.body: The measured gallop allows hold-up horses to close powerfully in the final 2f as the early leaders tire on testing ground. Patient rides on King Of The Dance and Charencey prove decisive as they sweep past weakening pace-setters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Homeland and Rival establish a clear lead and maintain their advantage
scenarios.body: The duo work together early then battle it out in the straight, with their fitness and tactical positioning proving too much for the closers. Soft ground blunts the finishing kick of hold-up horses who find too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Special
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawl
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 2f pole, suiting horses with natural speed who can quicken sharply. Whiskey Sunrise and Nutcracker benefit from their recent AW form translating to this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Homeland early causing pace to fracture
scenarios.body: Early speed duel creates gaps and opportunities for mid-division runners to pick up the pieces. The race splinters allowing an outsider to benefit from the chaos and slip through late.

watchPoints.text: Homeland's 187-day absence could see fitness lacking in the crucial final furlong despite tactical advantage
King Of The Dance and Charencey benefiting from patient rides if the pace becomes tactical as expected
Rival's prominent position early will indicate whether his lengthy absence has affected his usual racing style
Whiskey Sunrise and Nutcracker need to prove their recent AW form translates effectively to turf handicaps
Uncle Albert making stable debut for new connections but his fading tendency suggests watching rather than backing

races.name: Capital Windscreens Supporting Autistic Society Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 229-day break with early pace advantage but stamina questions over this trip
runners_data.comment: Off since beating one at Wolverhampton in October; needs to hit the ground running
runners_data.spotlight: Opened his account for current yard at Ffos Las (7f) in September but off since beating one in 7f Wolverhampton handicap following month; needs to hit the ground running on his seasonal return.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who goes well fresh but hasn't raced for 224 days and was difficult to settle last season
runners_data.comment: Scored at Leicester (6f) last May but she didn't prove the easiest to catch right after
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Leicester (6f) last May but she didn't prove the easiest to catch right later in 2025; has gone well fresh though, so not out of things on her seasonal return.

runners_data.name: Margorie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 7lb claiming jockey whose mark is dropping after recent poor form
runners_data.comment: Gained first win at Windsor in September but has failed to build on it since handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a first win at Windsor (6f) in September but she has failed to build on it since handicapping, ninth of 11 over 7f here 16 days ago; mark is falling but she still needs to take a big step forward.

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good current form, runner-up eight days ago off unchanged mark
runners_data.comment: 0-20 but he arrives in good nick; in the mix again off an unchanged mark
runners_data.spotlight: 0-20 but he arrives in good nick, second of 13 in 6f Brighton handicap eight days ago; well in the mix again off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Autumn Angel
runners_data.note: Recent course and distance winner up 3lb but had usual headgear removed for that success
runners_data.comment: Headgear left off when ending losing run over C&D latest; up 3lb but enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Had usual headgear left off when ending a long losing sequence over C&D 16 days ago; up 3lb but must enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Sub Thirteen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 5lb claimer who has been below par for new trainer Jeremy Scott
runners_data.comment: Fair 6f scorer for Tony Carroll but largely below par this season for his present handler
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer for Tony Carroll but largely below par this season for his present handler, 13th of 14 in 6f Windsor handicap two weeks ago; others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with blinkers replacing previous headgear, course winner but inconsistent this season
runners_data.comment: Course winner; twice failed to build on encouraging reappearance fourth at Wolverhampton
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner last May; has twice failed to build on an encouraging reappearance fourth at Wolverhampton in April so more is required here in a change of headgear.

runners_data.name: The Bear Of Saints
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 640 days off with fitness concerns despite gelding operation
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced maiden; off since September 2024 so has his fitness to prove for a new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden; not disgraced with fifth in 5.6f Bath maiden on his final run for Joe Tickle in September 2024; since gelded and has his fitness to prove on his comeback run for a new yard.

runners_data.name: Snuggle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for new trainer who shaped well on stable debut 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: Shaped well for new stable after ten months off with C&D fourth; not without interest
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer for Luke Dace in 2024; off ten months but shaped well for his new stable with fourth of 12 in C&D handicap 16 days ago; not without interest off a reduced mark.

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Front-runner with 7lb claimer whose recent form has declined significantly
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D scorer but his good form has dipped of late; needs to get back on track
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D scorer but his good form has dipped of late, beating only one at Wolverhampton (7f) last time; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Diamondsinthesand
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won three times in 2025 but yet to fire this season
runners_data.comment: A three-time winner in 2025 but yet to hit top form in a trio of runs this season
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time winner (around 6f) in 2025 but he's yet to hit top form in a trio of runs this season, seventh of 13 at Nottingham (5f) 18 days ago.

runners_data.name: Too Much Trevor
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with 5lb claimer in good current form, third here eight days ago
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in 30 attempts but she comes here in decent nick; back up 4lb now, though
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to score in 30 attempts but she comes here in decent nick, third of ten in 7f handicap here eight days ago; back up 4lb now, though.

races.paceDynamic: Kaleidoscope Eyes and Punchbowl Flyer will dispute the early lead, with Be An Angel, On Key, Autumn Angel, Snuggle and The Bear Of Saints all wanting prominent positions behind them. This creates significant congestion through the first 3f as seven horses fight for the front half of the field, before the genuine pace battle between the two leaders stretches the field. The strong early gallop will set up a tactical finish where those with the stamina to sustain their effort or the class to quicken late will prevail. This pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and benefit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Kaleidoscope Eyes and Punchbowl Flyer go hard early and the prominent brigade gets into a speed duel
scenarios.body: The pace collapses in the final furlong as the leaders tire, allowing patient hold-up horses to sweep past with superior finishing kicks. Margorie, Sub Thirteen, Ravenglass and Diamondsinthesand benefit most from this searching gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters moderate their speed and the prominent runners get perfect positions without over-racing
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of tactical speed rather than stamina, with those positioned handy but not committed able to kick clear. On Key and Autumn Angel are best placed to exploit this scenario from their ideal tracking positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If one of Kaleidoscope Eyes or Punchbowl Flyer establishes a clear lead while the prominent horses squabble behind
scenarios.body: The winner gets first run and holds on as the field fails to organize an effective pursuit until too late. Kaleidoscope Eyes has more natural pace and would be harder to peg back than the aging Punchbowl Flyer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes interference and checks in the straight as predicted
scenarios.body: Several fancied runners get hampered or have to switch around horses, allowing a freely-traveling outsider to steal through. The Bear Of Saints returning from a long break could benefit from a clear passage that others don't get.

watchPoints.text: Kaleidoscope Eyes and Punchbowl Flyer setting too strong an early pace and bringing stamina into play
Traffic problems developing 2f out as On Key, Autumn Angel, Be An Angel and Snuggle all converge from prominent positions
Margorie and Sub Thirteen getting clear runs from the back as both have claiming jockeys who may struggle in traffic
The Bear Of Saints handling the return from 21-month absence and whether fitness is there on debut for new connections
Autumn Angel coping with 3lb rise and racing without the headgear that was removed for his recent win

races.name: Capital Windscreens Supporting Mental Health Handicap

runners_data.name: Electric Bass
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose six second places suggest he's ready to strike, suited by the likely modest pace
runners_data.comment: 0-13 and has finished runner-up six times; in form and handles some ease in the ground
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 and his six runner-up placings may suggest something's afoot; did dead-heat at Kempton (1m4f, AW; demoted to second) in November and he comes here in form having chased one home again at Southwell in April and Bath last time; handles good to soft; can make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Port Of Entry
runners_data.note: Lightly raced but proven in France, needs to show more but prominent style suits this tactical setup
runners_data.comment: Fairly encouraging comeback for new yard but tailed off next time; tongue-tie added
runners_data.spotlight: Very lightly raced ex-French 6yo who didn't set the world alight for Andre Fabre in 2023, and after a fairly encouraging comeback for this yard at Kempton in April he was tailed off back there (also 2m, AW) one month later; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Baileys Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from long break faces tough task if pace doesn't develop strongly enough
runners_data.comment: Running poorly when last seen; mark fine if break has helped but easy turf is a query
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winning mare (2m, AW) but she was running poorly when last seen in the autumn; nothing wrong with this mark if the break has recharged her batteries but this is a rare turf outing and probably doesn't want too much rain.

runners_data.name: Bug Boy
runners_data.note: Course specialist returning from break, hold-up style needs strong gallop that may not materialise here
runners_data.comment: Course form figures of 21319 highlight two 1m4f wins; check market ahead of his return
runners_data.spotlight: Good record here down the years, with form figures of 21319 highlighting two wins at 1m4f (good); also scored twice over this trip in 2023 (including on good to soft) but no wins since and he only saw the track once last year; still worth a market check ahead of his return.

runners_data.name: Cloudside Rock
runners_data.note: Recent winner who needs genuine pace to showcase finishing kick, may struggle if tempo stays modest
runners_data.spotlight: Took ten goes to get off the mark but it was a convincing win at Ffos Las (1m4f, soft) in August and he doubled his tally when bagging Southwell handicap (1m3f, AW) on his April return; back up 4lb but he might be capable of better and holds leading claims.

runners_data.name: Marinakis
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer dropping in grade but tactical pace won't play to his strengths from this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Generally consistent in his time with Ian Williams when he scored three times on AW from 1m to 1m2f; second start for this yard wasn't devoid of promise at Kempton (1m4f) 17 days ago but suitability for the combination of this trip and likely ground is yet to be determined.

runners_data.name: Big Win
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form who should get ideal trip behind the leader, new yard going well
runners_data.comment: Good start for yard when second (1m6f, good to firm) latest; player despite ground query
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced at two; just five starts for Harry Charlton and following 18,000gns sale it was a good start for these connections when second at Bath (1m6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; likely softer ground is an unknown but he attracted support ahead of that stable debut and should cope with this drop back in trip; player.

runners_data.name: Rosco Rogers
runners_data.note: AW specialist making turf debut needs faster pace than likely here to show his best finishing speed
runners_data.comment: Last two runs were not good but maybe wind surgery/tongue-tie will help; rare turf start
runners_data.spotlight: AW campaigner who is having his first realistic go on turf; went close at Wolverhampton (9.5f) and Kempton (1m4f) in his first two handicaps but didn't progress across this winter's campaign; last two starts saw big defeats in the spring but maybe wind surgery will help and a tongue-tie is now added to his cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Wendy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who gets uncontested lead, modest form but race shape suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: Modest form in three qualifying runs; no surprise if she can do better in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Withdrawn from her intended debut last July on account of soft ground; modest form in three qualifying runs from 1m2f to 1m4f (AW/good) but starts her handicapping career at a modest level and no surprise if she can do better in this sphere; heed any market signals.

races.paceDynamic: Wonderful Wendy will lead from the start with no obvious challengers for the front rank, setting up a moderate tempo on ground that won't encourage extreme early pace. Electric Bass and Big Win are likely to sit prominent behind the leader, while Port Of Entry could also press forward if needed. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the leaders will control fractions, creating a race where those who can stay handy and have a turn of foot will be advantaged. This shape clearly favours prominent runners and those with tactical pace over pure hold-up horses who need a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Wendy sets uncontested fractions and the pace doesn't quicken significantly until the final 3f
scenarios.body: The early leaders maintain their advantage as hold-up horses struggle to make ground in the testing conditions. Prominent runners with stamina reserves prove hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling and creates a sprint finish from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the better quality hold-up horses to get into contention and produce their best finishing kicks. Class tells in a tactical finish where positioning becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Wendy gets easy fractions and has enough in reserve to resist late challenges
scenarios.body: The leader capitalises on the lack of pace pressure to control the race throughout and holds on grimly. Those who tried to close late pay for the slow early sections.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses refuse to commit early and the race becomes stop-start with multiple moves
scenarios.body: The messy tempo creates a lottery where those with the most tactical speed can quicken when it matters. Experience and racecraft become the deciding factors.

watchPoints.text: Wonderful Wendy's early pace setting - if she goes too slow she makes it a sprint, too fast and she stops
Electric Bass jumping and travelling in the first half-mile - his best efforts come when getting ideal positioning early
Big Win's adaptability to tactical pace having shown his best form in strongly run races recently
Cloudside Rock's position turning for home - needs to be closer than usual if pace stays moderate
Bug Boy's jumping and movement early - course winner needs to overcome rustiness from long absence
